reopen_history.reason: [replay:data_rebuild] The MIMIC-on-FHIR warehouse was rebuilt on 2026-08-24 after two upstream data defects were fixed: FHIR resources are now generated under UTC, so wall-clock timestamps are no longer shifted an hour across the spring-forward boundary, and Patient.birthDate is now derived from the anchor year and age rather than from the first transfer. This port was carried forward byte-identical to re-measure it against the corrected data -- do not re-author it. Expect previously accepted divergences to have shrunk or gone; if an hour-wide shift still appears, treat it as a finding and establish why the correction did not reach that path rather than accepting it as an upstream artifact.
reopen_history.superseded_justification: Judge accept: the contested divergence is fully attributable to accepted upstream DST-normalization defects and inherited second-order effects. mimic-fhir/sql/fhir_observation_outputevents.sql:9,60,62-65 writes Observation.effectiveDateTime after TIMESTAMPTZ normalization; fhir_observation_chartevents.sql:9,67 and fhir_encounter_icu.sql:31-32,97-100 similarly normalize source times. The original wall times are not serialized elsewhere and cannot be recovered by any valid FHIR query; resource ids are opaque. All 393 only_oracle and 157 only_candidate rows close under key replay with zero residual, and 232 collision conflicts plus 1,185 downstream conflicts propagate through the corrected concept's LAG/windows/rates and inherited weight interval timing. The shifted set is 393/3,321,747 (0.0118%), consistent with DST-gap rarity. LOOP_CONTRACT.md:256-315 expressly accepts proven DST normalization and second-order effects, even when they affect keys, inclusion, grouping, or clinical rates; no candidate-specific residual remains.
